demo.step3: Playtesting on phone, tablet and computer

s1.p: Paste your lesson text, upload a PDF, a picture or a text file, or describe what your class should practise, in your own words.

s2.p: It writes the game, then playtests it by itself on phone, tablet and computer sizes. Ask for changes in plain words: “make it harder”, “add a timer”.

builder.msg: Make a game from this lesson for my Year 5 class. Ten minutes, three levels, and end with the exit ticket questions.

cs.p: A full programme a teacher with no computing background can run: 45-minute lessons, each with a plan, a game chapter, a live warm-up and an exit ticket. CSTA levels 1B and 2.

b3.p: “One more round” feels like play, not a worksheet, so pupils practise more, without the weight of a mark.

faq.a1: A game-based learning platform for ages 5 to 14. Teachers turn their own lessons into interactive games with an AI Builder, run live class games, and use ready-made courses in maths, computing and online safety.
faq.a4: Almost any lesson: paste the text, upload a PDF, a picture or a text file, or describe the topic and what your class should practise. The Builder uses your material as a reference and makes a game around it.
